11. **FOS-000011 — Expose discovery and selection completeness.** **M; depends on `FOS-000009`; §2.** [stream scanning:1200](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/fossilize_db.cpp#L1200) intentionally salvages truncated tails (E9). Database composites may omit unavailable inputs; whitelists/ranges and replay-cache checks change observable work. Return preparation/discovery metadata: requested/opened inputs, excluded inputs/items with policy, selected logical scope, truncation/read failures, complete/unknown discovery. Keep salvage behavior and report its limits. **Check:** intact empty archive versus truncated archive with zero retained entries; missing optional versus required subdatabase; filters and ranges. Known processed items cannot establish full coverage when unread scope is unknown. A caller may explicitly accept a recovered prefix, but the report must name that scope.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Database/discovery integration tests:** E9 reports incomplete discovery even with zero retained items, while an intact empty archive reports known complete empty scope. The intact prefix remains readable; required missing/unreadable inputs prevent full-scope success.
   - **Selection/policy table tests:** Ranges, whitelists, deliberately optional inputs and explicitly accepted recovered-prefix policy report the exact selected/excluded scope and policy. Unknown unread totals remain unknown, never zero or full coverage; excluded items are not counted as failures or successes.

Legacy identity: `FOS-000012`. Original source: [immutable historical definition](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/73f891d6c0cf498ac92e804d7d0f0cd344a083f5/local-docs/reviews/observability-sweep.md).

## Original definition (verbatim)

12. **FOS-000012 — Reconcile final logical items across recovery attempts.** **M, split types/range-recovery if necessary; depends on `FOS-000009`, `FOS-000010`, `FOS-000011`; §2–§4.** Current atomics count activity and broad skips, while [condensed progress:71](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/fossilize_external_replayer.cpp#L71) explicitly clamps/weights counts and documents retry duplication. Preserve that UI estimate, but add authoritative accounting by selected `(tag, hash)` and attempt within a run/input scope. Distinguish selected work from extra dependencies and benchmark repetitions. Each selected item gets one final outcome; attempts retain their history. **Check:** duplicate/reordered messages, stale attempt failure after successful retry, one crash plus skipped culprit plus successful tail, unreported worker work. Do not infer exact successful counts by subtracting overlapping failure counters. Bound memory using range summaries/compact tables where possible; lost evidence must remain unknown.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Reconciliation model/property tests:** For a known selected set, every item has exactly one final outcome and final counts sum to that set. Permutations and duplicates of equivalent event histories yield the same final result; a stale failure cannot overwrite a newer authoritative success.
   - **Recovery and evidence-loss tests:** Failed attempt then complete retry succeeds with attempt history retained; skipped culprit plus successful tail remains incomplete. Lost reports retain unknown scope/counts. Extra dependencies, duplicate hashes across inputs and benchmark repetitions obey the declared identity rules without inflating selected-item counts.
   - **Bounded-state stress test:** Reconciliation of a generated large workload respects a documented state-size bound for the chosen representation; log sampling cannot alter authoritative accounting.

Legacy identity: `FOS-000013`. Original source: [immutable historical definition](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/73f891d6c0cf498ac92e804d7d0f0cd344a083f5/local-docs/reviews/observability-sweep.md).

## Original definition (verbatim)

13. **FOS-000013 — Publish one versioned replay result and derive exits from it.** **M; depends on `FOS-000003`, `FOS-000004`, `FOS-000005`, `FOS-000006`, `FOS-000007`, `FOS-000008`, `FOS-000009`, `FOS-000010`, `FOS-000011`, `FOS-000012`; §2–§5.** Introduce an explicit structured destination independent of verbosity, separate from stdout command payloads. Include declared policy/scope, execution completion, coverage, known/unknown reason counts, recovery and output status. Render the compact human failure summary from the same result. Document aggregate success/failure/invalid-invocation status; `1`/`2` is a reasonable choice, while internal child codes are a separate protocol. **Check:** controlled early failure, mixed categories, clean run, quiet workers, unwritable result destination and truncated output. Write a result with honest unavailable fields before waiting for every subsystem migration. Unknown completion of a required output prevents a success claim; later producer migrations improve the precision of that result. Completion publication must occur after required outputs; Linux currently sets `progress_complete` before identifier merging ([Linux:1383](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_linux.hpp#L1383)). Do not use the result mode to promise GPU cache durability.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Schema-validation and CLI contract tests:** Controlled early failures, mixed failures and success each deliver a complete versioned result matching the declared exit policy. Human and structured reports agree on outcome, scope and reasons; quiet mode retains the compact unsuccessful summary. Payload stdout remains valid command data.
   - **Delivery/order fault tests:** Unwritable, short-written or close-failed required result delivery cannot return zero. Hold a required output behind a test barrier: no successful final result/completion publication is observable before it finishes. Missing/truncated results are rejected as incomplete by a consumer fixture.
   - **Public contract fixtures:** Pin supported schema/reason/field/unit meanings and exit mappings, including the selected invalid-invocation code. Intentional changes to historical false-success exits are asserted as changes, not described as unchanged compatibility.

14. **FOS-000014 — Retain authoritative results independently of lossy progress events.** **M; depends on `FOS-000012`, `FOS-000013`; §4–§5.** [control block](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/fossilize_external_replayer_control_block.hpp#L29) explicitly permits drops; controller calls commonly ignore `shared_control_block_write()` failure. Preserve a final snapshot/result outside that informative ring, expose dropped-event counts, and add a result query to `ExternalReplayer`. Keep `wait()` process status and `poll_progress()` activity semantics distinguishable from the operation outcome. Version cookie/layout and producer/consumer compatibility need an explicit migration; do not append fields without auditing mapped-size assumptions. **Check:** saturated ring, no polling until exit, process death before final publication, delayed old attempt, old/new protocol mismatch. E6 must be diagnosable through the API with stdout/stderr discarded.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Transport saturation and API integration tests:** Fill the informative ring and defer polling until process exit: the retained authoritative result is still queryable, with diagnostic loss exposed. E6 is unsuccessful and diagnosable through the API with both standard streams discarded.
   - **Lifecycle/protocol compatibility tests:** Death before publication, delayed old attempts and repeated result queries cannot invent or overwrite an authoritative result. Old/new producer-consumer fixtures follow the documented compatibility matrix: supported combinations work, unsupported ones fail explicitly without accessing beyond the mapped layout.

Legacy identity: `FOS-000015`. Original source: [immutable historical definition](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/73f891d6c0cf498ac92e804d7d0f0cd344a083f5/local-docs/reviews/observability-sweep.md).

## Original definition (verbatim)

15. **FOS-000015 — Report cancellation and bound orderly shutdown reporting.** **M; depends on `FOS-000004`, `FOS-000009`, `FOS-000013`, `FOS-000014`; §3–§4.** Linux SIGINT/SIGTERM and sentinel closure call `shutdown_processes()` ([Linux:896](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_linux.hpp#L896), [Linux:1335](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_linux.hpp#L1335)); expected kills suppress crash treatment but do not establish completed work. Retain cancellation origin, unfinished scope and preserved outputs; preserve platform CLI termination conventions. From healthy control flow attempt the final result with bounded cleanup. Avoid adding allocation/locking/stdio serialization to fatal signal handlers: reuse minimal preallocated evidence and let the controller report. **Check:** user cancellation, parent/sentinel loss, forced kill during cleanup, blocked result channel. A missing final result is unknown, not successful. No final-report guarantee after SIGKILL.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Platform subprocess tests:** Controlled SIGINT/SIGTERM or the documented Windows cancellation equivalent, sentinel closure and forced cleanup termination preserve cancellation origin, completed/persisted work and unfinished scope. The CLI obeys the documented platform termination mapping; expected child kills are not classified as spontaneous crashes.
   - **Bounded-cleanup tests:** Block result delivery/cleanup through a test adapter and assert termination within the specified cleanup budget plus test tolerance. Kill before final publication and require the consumer to report incomplete/unknown; after publication, retain only facts already authoritative. No test assumes a final record after SIGKILL.

<!-- fossilize-migration-v1:FOS-000015 -->

Legacy identity: `FOS-000016`. Original source: [immutable historical definition](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/73f891d6c0cf498ac92e804d7d0f0cd344a083f5/local-docs/reviews/observability-sweep.md).

## Original definition (verbatim)

16. **FOS-000016 — Add database finalization that can report failure.** **M, one backend at a time; depends on `FOS-000003` and `FOS-000009`; §1, §6.** [DatabaseInterface:149](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/fossilize_db.hpp#L149) exposes void flush; [StreamArchive:1072](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/fossilize_db.cpp#L1072) ignores flush/close failures; [ZIP:776](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/fossilize_db.cpp#L776) only logs finalization failures during destruction. Provide explicit checked finalization before nonthrowing destruction and sticky I/O status with underlying error. Start with stream archives (E4), then directory/ZIP/concurrent wrappers. Preserve valid prefixes and define behavior after a partial entry write; do not blindly retry into a damaged tail. **Check:** buffered ENOSPC, partial write, ZIP finalize failure, child-backend failure, repeated finalize. Audit public virtual-interface compatibility: use a deliberate additive/versioned migration rather than casually breaking external implementations. Promise flush/close completion unless stronger durability is explicitly implemented.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Database-backend fault matrix:** For every migrated stream, directory, ZIP and concurrent backend, inject write, flush, close/finalize and delegated child errors. Explicit finalization returns a sticky originating failure before destruction; E4 returns nonzero after the CLI adopts the checked result.
   - **Recovery and ownership tests:** Repeated finalization follows the documented idempotence contract; destruction does not throw or double-close. After a partial entry failure, intact prior entries remain readable and later calls follow the documented stopped/recovery behavior rather than appending blindly to a damaged tail.
   - **Interface compatibility fixtures:** Compile/link an old-style external DatabaseInterface implementation against every API version claimed source-compatible. If binary compatibility is claimed, also run a prebuilt compatible consumer fixture; otherwise test explicit version rejection and document the break.

<!-- fossilize-migration-v1:FOS-000016 -->

17. **FOS-000017 — Expose recorder background completion and recording loss.** **M; depends on `FOS-000009` and `FOS-000016`; §1, §6.** [prepare:9117](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/fossilize.cpp#L9117) clears the database pointer on failure; writes throughout `record_task()` ignore bool results; [teardown:12530](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/fossilize.cpp#L12530) returns void. Add a queryable sticky recording outcome and an explicit completion operation. Distinguish accepted/queued, serialized, written and finalized; specify ownership so the recorder flushes borrowed databases while their owner performs close/finalization. Account separately for primary, identifier, last-use and pipeline-use outputs and intentional application filtering. **Check:** E1/E2, late close failure, failed hash/dependency resolution after acceptance, synchronized mode, multiple recorder sessions. Status must work with `LOG_NONE` and no callback; keep application Vulkan behavior unchanged.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Recorder tests with rejecting/mock databases:** E1/E2 remain accepted/queued when appropriate but completion/query reports the prepare/write loss with correct output role and affected scope. Inject delayed resolution, flush and owner-close failures; no accepted item is falsely certified persisted.
   - **Lifecycle/mode tests:** Background and synchronized modes, multiple sessions, intentional filters and failures in primary/identifier/last-use/pipeline-use outputs retain distinct outcomes. With LOG_NONE and no sink, outcomes remain queryable. The recorder never closes a borrowed database; owner finalization is explicitly combined with recording completion before claiming end-to-end persistence.

18. **FOS-000018 — Expose typed library operation reasons beyond the recorder.** **M, incremental entry points; depends on `FOS-000008`, `FOS-000009`, `FOS-000010`, `FOS-000011`, `FOS-000016`, `FOS-000017`; §1.** Public parse/record/database methods generally return bool, conflating unsupported state, corrupt input, missing dependency and I/O failure. Add result-bearing APIs while preserving compatibility wrappers where feasible. First cover `StateReplayer::parse` and recording rejection, then application-filter/database prepare/read/write. Include affected resource and known underlying error, not a mandatory prose parser. **Check:** same false result from incompatible version, unknown sType, missing referenced resource and write failure now produces distinct caller-actionable reasons. Callback absence must not erase these results. Queued `StateCreatorInterface` acceptance and eventual host-created object completion require an explicit contract; Fossilize cannot infer arbitrary host async success.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Public API contract tests:** Incompatible version, unknown sType, missing dependency, read/write failure and successful operations return distinct stable reasons with affected scope and raw details where known. Results are identical with callbacks absent or installed.
   - **Migration/async caller fixtures:** Legacy wrappers compile and match the documented bool mapping; any claimed ABI compatibility is tested separately. A fake StateCreatorInterface that accepts work and later fails demonstrates that queued acceptance cannot become host-object completion without the specified completion handshake. Unsupported legacy async evidence remains unknown.

19. **FOS-000019 — Publish capture completeness without changing application results.** **M; depends on `FOS-000017`, `FOS-000018`; §1–§2, §6.** [layer dispatch:1203](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/layer/dispatch.cpp#L1203) already preserves driver results across ordinary recording failures; build on that. [instance:509](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/layer/instance.cpp#L509) creates/configures the recorder but has no persistent capture-outcome interface. Add per-recorder/application scope status, explicit filtered/disabled state, missing resources and finalization outcome, then a documented query/report mechanism owned by the layer/integrator. **Check:** Vulkan success plus capture failure, capture unsupported feature, failed prepare, concurrent instances/devices and teardown. Do not conflate application compilation failure with recording loss. The opt-in emergency-dump modes intentionally alter signal handling; retain and disclose that mode rather than claiming every current mode guarantees host continuity.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Layer integration tests using a controlled Vulkan dispatch:** When the driver succeeds and capture prepare/record/finalization fails, the application receives the same Vulkan result and valid handles as the capture-disabled control; queryable capture status reports the separate loss. When the driver fails, its raw result is preserved without inventing capture success.
   - **Capture lifetime/isolation tests:** Concurrent instances/devices keep scope and outcomes isolated; filtered/disabled capture, unsupported recording, teardown and failed finalization remain distinguishable. Ordinary operation continues after recoverable capture faults. Emergency-dump mode is explicitly identified and tested separately from ordinary continuity guarantees.

FOS-000020.body:
Legacy identity: `FOS-000020`. Original source: [immutable historical definition](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/73f891d6c0cf498ac92e804d7d0f0cd344a083f5/local-docs/reviews/observability-sweep.md).

Shared requirements and grouping: https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/8. All original criteria below remain required. Source status statements below describe their historical revision; current delivery evidence is recorded separately. Original relative links are resolved below.

## Original definition (verbatim)

20. **FOS-000020 — Make library presentation optional and define callback safety.** **M; depends on `FOS-000017`, `FOS-000018`, `FOS-000019` for log-independent truth; §1, §5.** A callback and inherited recorder-thread configuration already exist in [errors:42](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/fossilize_errors.hpp#L42), with tests. [callback:12666](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/fossilize.cpp#L12666) calls the sink synchronously with borrowed stack text; direct LOG calls in database bucket setup/application filtering bypass this route. Document thread/lifetime/reentrancy rules; route recoverable library presentation through the optional host sink and audit direct stderr fallbacks. Avoid invoking user callbacks under internal locks; provide recursion protection and explicit truncation/drop accounting. Exception-enabled builds need containment; default builds disable exceptions. **Check:** no sink/no unsolicited streams, reentrant callback, throwing callback where enabled, expired userdata prevention by contract, long messages. A timeout cannot safely preempt an arbitrary C++ callback: use an explicit nonblocking sink contract or a bounded queued delivery mode, not an impossible guarantee.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Diagnostic routing and callback tests:** Library operations with no sink produce no unsolicited stdout/stderr under the chosen presentation contract while retaining operation outcomes. Installed callbacks receive documented thread context and borrowed-data lifetime; a controlled reentrant callback does not deadlock or recurse without bound.
   - **Failure/lifetime tests:** Exception-enabled builds contain a throwing sink; exception-disabled builds compile and pass applicable cases. A synchronized unregister/drain or other documented lifetime protocol prevents callbacks after userdata release. Oversized messages disclose truncation, and optional sink loss cannot change Vulkan results.
   - **Delivery-mode tests:** If queued delivery is provided, block the consumer and assert bounded queue memory, nonblocking production and exposed drops. If synchronous delivery is retained, test compliant nonblocking callbacks and explicitly scope the guarantee; do not claim safe preemption of an arbitrary blocking callback.

21. **FOS-000021 — Propagate required-output failures and preserve merge evidence.** **M, one output family per change; depends on `FOS-000003`, `FOS-000013`, `FOS-000016`, `FOS-000017`; §2, §6.** [pipeline-cache export:1835](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay.cpp#L1835) loses retrieval/write/close outcomes; [stats CSV:4053](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay.cpp#L4053) silently returns on open failure; `dump_stats()` has no returned outcome. Identifier merging logs failure and then removes child archives ([Linux:1417](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_linux.hpp#L1417), analogous Windows). Define which requested outputs are required and make their failure affect the final result. Remove source artifacts only after checked successful merge/publication; retain recoverable parts otherwise. **Check:** missing directory, ENOSPC at close, Vulkan cache-data retrieval failure, one malformed stats shard, merge failure. No success publication before required exports finish. Optional telemetry failure remains distinct from required output failure.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Required/optional output integration matrix:** Inject cache-data retrieval, open, write, flush/close, malformed-shard and merge failures. Every required-output failure yields an unsuccessful aggregate with output identity; otherwise successful work with optional telemetry loss keeps its declared operation outcome and exposes the loss separately.
   - **Filesystem preservation/order tests:** A failed merge/publication leaves original child archives and any valid destination intact according to the declared replacement policy. A successful checked publication permits cleanup. Barrier tests prove successful completion is never published before all required exports/finalization finish.

22. **FOS-000022 — Describe reuse evidence and compatibility honestly.** **M; depends on `FOS-000006`, `FOS-000011`, `FOS-000012`, `FOS-000013`, `FOS-000014`, `FOS-000021`; §5–§6.** Report separate facts for replayer-cache marker skips ([replay:3144](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay.cpp#L3144)), application pipeline-cache feedback ([replay:1479](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay.cpp#L1479)), shader identifiers and opaque driver-managed caches. Include build/tool version, input identities, effective filters/options, null-device mode, device/driver/API and relevant UUID context, deadlines and duration units. Existing GPU and timing logs are useful but not a retained structured context record. **Check:** unavailable feedback stays unknown, simulated null-device run cannot claim GPU warming, legacy markers do not prove persistence, changed device/driver context is visible. Metadata alone is not proof of cache hits. Steam's scheduling rationale remains outside Fossilize's evidence.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Context and evidence-classification tests:** Marker skip, reported application-cache hit/miss, shader identifier and unavailable driver-cache feedback remain separate fields/facts. Null-device success cannot claim GPU warming; legacy markers, replay success and checked close cannot claim verified reuse or power-loss durability.
   - **Deterministic context fixtures and hardware integration:** Reports preserve known version/input/filter/device/driver/API/UUID/deadline context with explicit unknowns and fixed duration units; changing context changes the relevant identity fields. A registered hardware job asserts feedback facts on a capable device. Missing hardware is reported skipped/unverified, never as a passing cache-reuse test.

23. **FOS-000023 — Migrate remaining CLI contracts and internal consumers.** **M, separate small tool changes; depends on `FOS-000002`, `FOS-000013`, `FOS-000016`, `FOS-000017`, `FOS-000018`, `FOS-000021`, `FOS-000022`; §2–§6.** Extend result/exit/output conventions to convert/merge, opt/disasm, prune/rehash, synth, bench, feature-sifter and cache-roundtrip validation. Conversion and merge already check many immediate bool failures; add missing phase/resource details and checked finalization, not a wholesale rewrite. [roundtrip:230](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_validate_cache_roundtrip.cpp#L230) parses console prose for hits/misses; consume versioned results instead. Explicitly reject mixed misses when the roundtrip policy requires all hits (current branch only rejects zero hits plus nonzero misses). [bench:296](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_bench.cpp#L296) returns `EXIT_FAILURE` from a bool function, converting failure to true. **Check:** each tool's success, invalid invocation, partial/unsupported work and output-delivery failure; optimizer fallback policy and intentional pruning remain explicit. Keep list payloads on stdout and reports separate. Structured results must cover controlled failures too, not only the successful end path.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Registered per-tool CLI contract suite:** For each supported target, assert success, invalid invocation, partial/unsupported work and required-output failure against its documented policy, result schema and exit mapping. Verify payload/report stream separation, intentional prune exclusions and optimizer fallback behavior. Hardware-dependent cases use mocks plus separately registered hardware jobs.
   - **Internal consumer regressions:** Roundtrip validation uses structured fields and works when prose is disabled/changed; under an all-hits policy, all hits pass while mixed hits/misses, all misses and absent/unknown feedback fail. The benchmark read-error fixture returns false. Existing supported invocation fixtures still run, with intentional behavior changes explicitly asserted.

24. **FOS-000024 — Bound diagnostics without sampling away outcomes.** **M, subsystem increments; depends on `FOS-000009`, `FOS-000012`, `FOS-000013`, `FOS-000014`, `FOS-000020`; §4–§5.** [spam limiting:88](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/fossilize_errors.hpp#L88) already bounds several call sites, but static counters span calls/recorders and only expose a silencing message; many CLI failures log per item. Add per-run/session reason totals, bounded examples, sampled/dropped/truncated counts and event severity/time. Keep these independent of authoritative final item accounting. Make expensive timing/tracing opt-in and avoid baseline shader dumps, environment values or sensitive absolute paths; retain a caller-controlled path/detail policy. **Check:** many repeated failures, multiple runs in one process, ring overload, long messages and blocked/failed sink. Require bounded baseline memory/overhead and the same final counts with verbose logging enabled or disabled. Establish measurements before picking performance budgets.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Diagnostic/accounting stress tests:** For N repeated failures above the sample cap, authoritative reason/item counts remain correct while examples/queue state respect documented numeric caps; sampled/dropped/truncated counts explain loss. Repeating runs in one process resets session-local budgets and counters.
   - **Privacy/verbosity tests:** Run the same workload with diagnostics off, normal and verbose: final outcomes/counts are identical. Sentinel shader text, secret environment values and sensitive paths do not appear in baseline outputs under the chosen detail policy. Events carry valid severity/time and preserve documented units.
   - **Automated resource-budget check:** Before completing this item, define measurable baseline memory/overhead limits and a reproducible benchmark configuration. The registered benchmark enforces those limits with documented tolerance; expensive tracing is disabled by default. A blocked/failing sink cannot cause unbounded buffering or alter operation results.

Legacy identity: `FOS-000025`. Original source: [immutable historical definition](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/73f891d6c0cf498ac92e804d7d0f0cd344a083f5/local-docs/specs/basic-change-harness-plan.md).

Shared requirements and grouping: https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/9. All original criteria below remain required. Source status statements below describe their historical revision; current delivery evidence is recorded separately. Original relative links are resolved below.

## Original definition (verbatim)

# Basic change harness: proposed skill design

Date: 2026-10-27. Status: FOS-000025 v1 implementation merged in
[PR #2](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/pull/2). Historical acceptance
describes that revision; subsequent changes require their own verification.

## Outcome and boundaries

Create a discoverable repository skill named `implement-change-harness`. It runs one
identified root task at a time in this repository, with sequential, independently
verifiable subtasks when necessary. It produces one verified implementation branch
and one pull request to `master` for the whole task. It does not merge the PR,
schedule itself, discover another task, or implement unrelated improvements.

The parent agent coordinates. Planning, implementation and adversarial checking
each run in a fresh subagent. The coordinator manages durable state and publishing;
it does not replace a failed checker with its own judgment.

## FOS-000025 — Implement the change harness skill

Canonical task definition. Status: Done (merged in [PR #2](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/pull/2)). Implement the workflow specified
below as a tracked, discoverable skill with a standard-library state/Git helper,
meaningful automated tests and independently checked evidence. Preserve the
planner/implementer/checker responsibilities and per-subtask verification gates.
Acceptance requires tested state transitions, recovery and publication safeguards,
a validated skill package, and one PR to robinwassen/Fossilize master. Use this
three-role method to implement the harness itself; record the bootstrap run on
harness-artifacts before dispatching agents. Product C++ changes are out of scope.

Completion evidence (historical FOS-000025 only): the retained independent
`checker-final` accepted `e01fa9d68ade5384f214ec46a6ddc352b22a03de` against base
`bbe8ae4acd9ad527658bb58e6b06474924a06284`: 27 discovered/executed tests, no skips,
and passed skill metadata validation. The completed local run
`runs/FOS-000025/2026-10-27-bootstrap` records PR #2 and successful attachment.
GitHub reports merge `35a72926c8e313a11c8de5ce61c1356cbfa4eccd` on 2026-10-27.
These historical executions do not verify FOS-000026 or later revisions.

AGENTS.md and local-docs are shared in Git.

## Lessons applied from the requested lecture

The lecture argues for external memory, separation of implementation and judgment,
explicit stopping conditions, bounded context, and starting with a small system.
Those become committed state, independent checker attempts, evidence gates, fresh
agent contexts, and a sequential workflow. These are design choices, not a claim
that multiple agents guarantee correctness. Different models can share blind spots.

Do not adopt scheduling or an endless research loop: this change workflow has a
finite outcome. Do not use PR counts or passing test counts as quality measures.

Source: https://walkinglabs.github.io/learn-harness-engineering/en/lectures/lecture-13-loop-engineering/

## Repository layout and branches

- Implementation: `codex/<root-key>-<short-description>` from the recorded target
  `master` commit, in a dedicated worktree. Preserve the user's checkout and edits.
- Artifacts: `harness-artifacts`, created as an orphan branch with an empty root
  tree. Subsequent commits contain only harness records, never a source-tree copy.
  Use a separate artifacts worktree. Never merge this branch into `master` or the
  implementation branch. Verify an existing branch before adopting it.
- Planner: a detached worktree at the planning input commit.
- Checker: a fresh detached worktree at the exact candidate commit for each check.
  Keep test outputs out of tracked source files and use separate build directories.
- All worktrees are in the same Git repository; this is procedural isolation and
  context separation, not a security sandbox. Agents still share filesystem access.

Artifacts branch contents:

```text
active.json                              # one active run pointer, or null
allocations.json                         # permanent issued/reserved key journal
runs/<root-key>/<run-id>/state.json       # canonical current run state
runs/<root-key>/<run-id>/reports/...      # planner/implementer/checker reports
runs/<root-key>/<run-id>/evidence/...     # small logs and evidence metadata
```

JSON is proposed instead of YAML to use Python's standard library and eliminate a
parser dependency. Both plans remain structured fields inside state.json. Git
history preserves previous plans and transitions; reports retain detailed findings.
Avoid storing full transcripts, build trees, binaries or secret-bearing raw logs.

Default PR destination for this checkout: `robinwassen/Fossilize`, base `master`,
using `origin`. `upstream` points to ValveSoftware/Fossilize; do not select it merely
because it is upstream. Record repository identity explicitly at initialization.
Publishing artifacts is a separate policy: default local-only, with its lack of
cross-machine recovery made explicit. Pushing implementation is required for a PR.

## Task keys and canonical definitions

The root uses its existing permanent backlog key. New root tasks must first be
registered under the project rules. Every split-out subtask also receives a new
project-wide key; array positions and run IDs are not task keys.

For Fossilize, allocate `FOS-` followed by at least six digits, above every previously
issued number. Inspect the registry and all current/archived backlog definitions.
Register allocations in local-docs/backlog-keys.md before creating definitions.
Never recycle keys. Reserve interrupted allocations permanently rather than fill gaps.

The existing root backlog remains canonical; state stores its key, location and
input snapshot. Harness-created subtasks have their canonical definition in tracked local-docs
on the implementation branch, with that location in the registry. Artifacts
retain execution/acceptance records and reference the canonical source definition.
FOS-000026 supersedes the former artifact-only subtask definition rule; legacy
units require explicit location migration before closeout. Other mentions
are references, not additional definitions. Retire or preserve keys on replanning;
do not reinterpret an old subtask key as a different task.

The tracked registry is the project allocation authority. Agents propose
decomposition; the coordinator allocates keys under the repository lock and
includes registry updates with the implementation branch. Reconcile allocations
from unmerged harness runs before allocating; a branch snapshot alone may be stale.
Worktrees read the tracked guidance from their input revision, with explicit paths
to newer required guidance when necessary. Independent clones/machines are outside
v1's serialization guarantee; concurrent remote allocations require coordination.

Preserve a minimal permanent allocation journal/high-water mark on the artifacts
branch as well as the tracked project registry. Before allocating, reconcile the union
of both records and all backlog definitions; never trust only one counter. Write
the reservation durably first, then update the tracked registry, then publish the
subtask definition. Interrupted reservations remain issued forever. The journal
contains key/location/allocation metadata, not copies of the project guidance.
Conflicting meanings for one key require reconciliation rather than renumbering.
The registered ledger currently reaches FOS-000025; re-read it at allocation time rather
than encoding the next number in the skill.

## Agent contracts and bounded context

Use `fork_turns="none"` on every phase/attempt. Supply repository/worktree paths,
root key, current subtask, immutable input commit, plan version, acceptance criteria,
relevant guidance paths and the expected report format. Agents read only the
additional files needed for their task. All three agents must read applicable
AGENTS.md instructions and the required project index, descriptor and pillars.
Read relevant specifications without claiming desired properties are proven behavior.
Before planning or running verification, read the testing guide referenced by
AGENTS.md: for this project, local-docs/verification.md. Make this guide available
to all three roles from the tracked project documentation. Follow its links
selectively; do not copy its entire test inventory into every worker prompt.

Do not pass the full parent transcript. Reports are concise summaries with evidence
paths. A retry gets unresolved findings and relevant decisions rather than its
predecessor's entire conversation. No nested delegation in v1.

### Planner

Read the root request, backlog definition, relevant code and project guidance.
Return the problem, expected behavior, explicit non-goals, affected boundaries,
implementation plan, verification plan, risks and assumptions.

The planner owns test planning, including which tests the suite must be extended
with for each subtask. Specify the existing tests to reuse or modify, new test
cases and fixtures, intended test files/targets, relevant runner registration,
and the behavior and assertions each test must exercise. For regression fixes,
plan evidence that the test detects the original defect where feasible. If no
suite extension is needed, explain how existing coverage establishes the required
behavior. Record these decisions in the versioned verification plan before
implementation; the checker does not take over test planning.

Each subtask must have a coherent outcome, dependencies, intended changes and
acceptance evidence that can be obtained before advancing. A test-file edit and its
implementation normally belong together. Prefer no decomposition for a small fix.
An original reproducer or baseline failure is included where feasible.

Verification covers positive behavior, relevant failure/unsupported cases,
regressions, scope boundaries and environment requirements. Commands include their
working directories and expected results. Where runtime checks are not practical,
specify the review evidence and the remaining uncertainty. Do not invent hardware
access or downgrade a required hardware check to optional after it fails.

The planner selects and justifies the important checks for each subtask using the
project testing guide and the actual changed behavior. Record a verification gate
for each acceptance criterion: the risk/behavior addressed, check method, exact
command/cwd or review procedure, fixture, prerequisites/environment, expected
assertions, and evidence to retain. Classify checks as required for this subtask,
required at final integration, or optional diagnostic checks. Explain exclusions
when an apparently relevant testing category is intentionally omitted. Existing
project-mandated checks remain mandatory; planner judgment cannot remove them.

Prefer the smallest checks that establish the required behavior, with relevant
negative/regression cases. For example, a CPU-only database fix can require an
assertion-bearing persistence-failure regression and relevant system tests without
requiring a real Steam game. A claim about real driver compilation needs suitable
driver evidence; null-device replay does not establish it. An empty CTest run or
successful build cannot satisfy a behavioral test gate. Interactive, expensive or
environment-mutating checks follow the guide's scope and authorization boundaries.

Resolve unavailable prerequisites during planning where possible. If a mandatory
gate cannot run, record the limitation and route it for an environment or scope
decision. Optional checks may remain unavailable with an explanation. Subtask
completion requires all its mandatory gates to pass; defer only explicitly planned
whole-task checks to final integration. The checker may require additional checks
for concrete uncovered risks, routing acceptance/plan changes through the planner.

The coordinator validates the plan's completeness and unique keys mechanically.
Planner and implementation output cannot silently weaken the original task.

### Implementer

Take at most one ready subtask. Implement its source changes and planned test-suite
additions or modifications, register tests with the relevant runner where needed,
and run the required checks. Iterate locally, then commit a candidate including
the tests and return the SHA, changes, results and limitations. Map each planned
test to its implemented location and actual execution evidence; explain omissions
as incomplete work rather than silently skipping them.
Only this role edits implementation source and committed tests; it cannot certify acceptance or edit
canonical state, acceptance requirements or verifier reports.

Do not proceed to the next subtask until the checker accepts this one. A rejected
candidate returns to implementation with actionable findings. An infeasible plan
returns to the planner through the coordinator; unrelated discoveries are recorded
as out-of-scope observations rather than automatically implemented.

### Checker

Start fresh at the candidate SHA. First derive expected behavior from the original
task and project constraints; then consult the plans and implementer's factual
report. Independently inspect the full relevant diff, rerun decisive checks and
probe credible counterexamples. Check for unrelated changes and weakened tests.

Validate that the planned test-suite extensions were correctly implemented and
actually run. Inspect test assertions, fixtures, failure injection and runner
registration, and confirm the tests exercise the intended behavior rather than
passing vacuously or testing only a mock. Independently run the required gates at
the candidate SHA, verify that the intended tests were discovered/executed, and
retain actual results. Check evidence that regression tests detect the original
defect where required by the plan. An implementer's success report, a build, an
empty test run or skipped tests cannot substitute for that evidence.

Incorrect or missing implementation of an already planned test returns to the
implementer. Missing coverage in the plan returns to the planner for a versioned
update, then to the implementer and a fresh checker. The checker reports the gap
and evidence; the planner owns the resulting test design and gate changes.

Return `accepted`, `changes_required`, or `unable_to_verify`, with criterion-level
evidence, findings and residual uncertainty. Findings include file/location,
concrete failure scenario and relevance to acceptance. Acceptance is not a vote or
a lack of findings. It requires evidence for every required criterion.

The checker may construct disposable probes in its own worktree; any proposed
source or test fix goes back to the implementer and is checked again. It does not
modify the candidate branch. A check verifies a specific candidate/base/plan tuple.
It also assesses whether the planner selected sufficient gates for the original
requirements. Passing a weak plan is not acceptance. Missing necessary coverage
returns to planning; the implementer cannot waive a gate or redefine its result.

After all subtasks are accepted, run a fresh whole-task check on the combined
branch. Earlier subtask acceptance alone does not establish integration correctness.

## Model and effort policy

Initial, configurable proposal; validate against the live runtime's model catalog:

| Role | Model | Effort | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| Coordinator | Current parent model | Inherited | Small routing/state context |
| Planner | gpt-6.1-sol | high | Bound scope and choose meaningful evidence |
| Implementer | gpt-6.1-sol | medium | Focused, sequential changes |
| Checker | gpt-6.1-sol | high | Counterexamples and independent verification |

Raise implementation effort for C++ lifetime, concurrency, Vulkan compatibility,
serialization or unclear failure behavior. Permit a stronger available model for
an unresolved reasoning problem, within the recorded budget. Do not automatically
select the most expensive effort, or a cheaper checker because its report is short.
Model diversity is optional; independent evidence matters more than model names.

Store requested and actual model/effort on every attempt. Validate support before
dispatch; do not silently substitute unavailable models. Use an explicitly recorded
supported fallback or record a capability blocker. Do not change global Codex config.

Official reference: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/subagents

## Durable state contract

Use a versioned schema with these required field groups:

| Group | Contents |
|---|---|
| Identity | schema version, state revision, run ID, root key, canonical task location, input snapshot |
| Repository | repo identity/common Git directory, target remote/repository/master SHA, implementation branch/worktree and candidate SHA |
| Progress | phase, operation, status, active subtask key, next action, stop/blocker reason |
| Plan | version, original acceptance requirements, scope/non-goals, implementation plan, verification plan including per-subtask test-suite extensions and required gates |
| Subtasks | unique keys, canonical definitions, dependencies, criteria, status, accepted SHA and evidence references |
| Attempts | role, attempt ID, worker ID, input SHA/plan/revision, model/effort, timestamps, result/report references |
| Verification | exact candidate and base SHA, plan version, planned-test-to-implementation mapping, discovered/executed tests, commands/cwd, environment, exit/result, log reference, criterion coverage |
| Findings | unique finding IDs, affected task key, evidence, resolution and recheck result |
| Limits | implementation/repair/replan counts, command timeouts, run time budget, usage when available |
| Publishing | destination, head/base, persisted intent, remote head, PR identity/URL, attach outcome |

Keep phase separate from status. Three agent phases are `planning`, `implementing`
and `checking`. Administrative phases are `initializing` and `publishing`, followed
by `complete`. Status expresses `ready`, `running`, `interrupted`,
`awaiting_decision`, `failed` or `complete`; the checking operation distinguishes
subtask from final verification. A blocked run records its exact resumption action.

Evidence distinguishes passed, failed, unsupported, incomplete and not-run results.
Unsupported or incomplete mandatory verification cannot produce acceptance.

## State transitions and recovery

1. Acquire a repository-wide OS lock in the common Git directory; inspect active
   run, branches, worktrees, tools, model support and local guidance. Resume an
   existing run instead of starting another root task.
2. Initialize durable identity and record the target base. Persist each dispatch
   intent before starting its worker; persist worker identity immediately after
   creation. Validate the report before recording a result or advancing.
3. Planner -> implementer -> checker. On rejection, return the same subtask to
   implementation. On acceptance, select the next ready subtask. After the last
   subtask, perform final checking, then publishing.
4. The coordinator is the only writer of canonical state. A helper validates legal
   transitions and expected state revision, atomically writes state, and commits
   state plus reports to harness-artifacts. The Git ref is the durable checkpoint;
   uncommitted artifact files do not advance a phase.
5. On resume, reconcile durable intent with actual agents/processes, source HEAD,
   dirty/untracked files, artifact commits, evidence and remote PR state. Preserve
   partial work. Do not blindly restart a command, reset a worktree, or adopt an
   unrecorded commit as accepted.
6. A stale lock is not proof a worker stopped. Confirm prior writers terminated
   before dispatching replacements. Uncertainty becomes awaiting_decision. Tag
   reports with attempt IDs and input revisions; reject late/stale results. The
   dispatch-before-worker-ID crash window requires explicit reconciliation and
   must be covered by a recovery test.
   Record an unacknowledged dispatch as an ambiguous outcome, not an absent worker.
   Use the runtime's actual worker cancellation/status facilities. If they cannot
   establish termination, stop for intervention before starting a replacement.
7. Changed source invalidates prior final acceptance. A changed plan invalidates
   affected acceptance. If target master advances, refresh the integration baseline
   under a recorded policy and rerun affected checks before publishing; conflicts
   return to implementation. Do not claim a proof against future target commits.

Proposed bounds: initial candidate plus at most three repair rounds per subtask,
one replan per run, with separate command and run timeouts recorded before work.
Repeated identical failures without new evidence stop early. Budget exhaustion
records unfinished work and the next action; it never masquerades as success.
Infrastructure errors do not automatically become code failures. Resume requires
an explicit budget extension when the configured budget is exhausted.

## Publishing and completion

Require all planned subtasks accepted, no unresolved acceptance findings, a final
checker acceptance for the current candidate/base/plan, and all required checks
passed. Required CI belongs in that gate if it can run before PR creation; if the
host requires a PR to run CI, distinguish PR opened from CI-verified completion
and record that policy before execution.

Persist PR creation intent, push the implementation branch, verify its remote SHA,
then look up an existing PR by exact target repository, base and head before
creating one. An ambiguous network failure triggers lookup, not immediate retry.
Include closed and merged PRs in that lookup; never silently reopen or replace a
closed PR. Reconcile the discovered outcome with the run's identity and state.
Record the URL and attach it to the current Codex chat with attach_artifact.
An attachment failure retries attachment without creating another PR.

One PR covers the root and all subtasks. Never create a subtask PR. Default to a
ready-for-review PR after verification; use a draft only if the task requests it
or a recorded repository policy requires it. No automatic merge or force push.
Complete means verified and PR opened, not merged. A publication failure retains
the verified candidate and resumes publishing without reimplementing it.

Write the PR description in plain language with these explicit level-two Markdown
section headings, even for a small change. Keep the content proportional to scope:

- `## Problem`: describe the affected user/workflow and the observable problem.
- `## What changes`: explain behavior before and after the change.
- `## Why this matters`: explain why this matters in terms of the project's purpose.
- `## Why this approach`: explain why this approach and scope were chosen, including a meaningful
  alternative or tradeoff when relevant, without a transcript of deliberation.
- `## Verification and limits`: say what was checked and where uncertainty remains.
- `## Task references`: list root/subtask keys with links to the tracked backlog and sufficient standalone context.

Do not put private machine configuration, full run transcripts or inaccessible evidence
links into the public PR. Supply sufficient public explanation and verification.

## Skill package and implementation sequence

Tracked destination: `.agents/skills/implement-change-harness/`. This repository
skill travels with agent worktrees. An optional personal symlink may expose the
same package elsewhere, but must not replace an existing user skill.

```text
SKILL.md                       # purpose, invariants, coordinator routing
agents/openai.yaml             # discovery metadata
references/roles.md             # three bounded role contracts
references/state.md             # schema, transitions, recovery, publication rules
scripts/harness_state.py        # validated state and artifact-branch operations
scripts/test_harness_state.py   # meaningful recovery/invariant tests in temp repos
```

Keep role-specific material out of unrelated workers' prompts. Prefer one small
standard-library helper over a daemon, database, scheduler or custom agent runtime.
The helper manages deterministic mechanics; Codex handles agent orchestration and
project-specific implementation/verification. No pretending the skill alone is a
durable background service: it resumes when invoked again after a session ends.

Implementation order: (1) settle the policy decisions below; (2) implement and
test schema/Git/checkpoint mechanics; (3) write coordinator and role contracts;
(4) validate skill metadata; (5) simulate worker reports and interrupted runs in
temporary repositories; (6) run one small real task after creation is requested.
Do not open a real PR merely to test the skill's publication code.

## Adversarial validation scenarios

- A second invocation cannot start a different root task while one is active.
- Root/subtask key collisions, absent registrations, retired-key reuse, dangling
  dependencies and cyclic dependencies are rejected.
- Each interruption boundary resumes without skipping verification, discarding
  partial source changes, duplicating workers, or duplicating a PR.
- Stale/late worker reports and verdicts for the wrong SHA/base/plan are rejected.
- The implementation agent reports success but the original reproducer still fails;
  the checker rejects it. A deliberately weakened test does not satisfy acceptance.
- A planned test is omitted, unregistered, skipped or vacuous; the checker rejects
  the candidate despite a passing build or suite exit. A missing test design goes
  back to the planner; an incorrectly implemented planned test goes to implementation.
- A later subtask breaks an earlier one; final whole-task checking rejects it.
- A required GPU/driver check is unavailable; the result stays incomplete.
- PR creation succeeds but the connection fails before state records the URL;
  resume finds the one existing PR. Remote push/branch conflicts preserve work.
- master changes or a user edits source after checking; stale acceptance cannot
  publish the changed candidate as verified.
- Artifact writes fail or state is malformed; no phase advances or success claim.
- Artifact branch contains only records, and source PRs contain no harness records
  or private machine configuration. Original checkout remains untouched.
- Repeated rejection, exhausted budgets and unclear worker liveness stop with a
  precise recoverable state rather than looping or declaring success.

The v1 candidate implements these mechanics in a standard-library helper and
assertion-bearing tests using temporary Git repositories and a local bare remote.
The exact planned-case mapping and executed results belong to the run's reports;
the test descriptions here do not establish that a particular candidate passed.
The actual fresh-role run and independent final check are separate evidence from
unit tests. Syntax validation alone is insufficient.

An independent design-review subagent identified the surviving-worker and ambiguous
dispatch windows, the allocation-ledger durability gap, stale approvals after replans,
the moving-base publication window, and the need for a single authoritative Git
checkpoint. The proposal incorporates those corrections. The review is a design
exercise. The implementation candidate addresses these cases; its independent
checker must establish which guarantees the observed evidence supports.

## V1 mechanics and explicit limits

The [tracked skill](../../.agents/skills/implement-change-harness/SKILL.md) documents
the actual CLI, role contracts and schema. The helper has finite explicit actions;
it does not call agents, run arbitrary shell commands or access GitHub. The
coordinator performs those operations and records actual observations.

Git plumbing builds records in a temporary index, creates a commit and advances
`harness-artifacts` with an expected-old-tip compare-and-swap. The committed ref is
the authority. An artifact worktree remains an inspectable, possibly stale view;
its index and edits cannot override a committed checkpoint. Never discard its
unexpected edits merely to refresh the view. Locking uses POSIX advisory `flock`
in the common Git directory and covers cooperative writers on this machine only.
Other platforms and distributed key allocation are unsupported by this v1.

An unsplit root is its own work unit without another canonical definition. Report
identity binds to the dispatch input revision, even after worker acknowledgement
increments state. Structured evidence validation checks completeness and identity;
semantic assertion quality and actual role conduct still require an independent
checker. Deadline checks occur on helper invocation, with the coordinator enforcing
recorded command timeouts; there is no background watchdog.

The original bootstrap schema is deliberately incomplete. Explicit import retains
Git history, original requirements, legacy worker/report facts and uncertainty,
normalizes known commit identities and starts the budget at the first state commit.
A known completed implementer's candidate may be imported only as unverified.
Import requires reconciliation of every known legacy worker before a replacement
or fresh checker. A live bootstrap lock owner must release the lock before helper
handoff; deleting the lock file is not a handoff.

For this skill-only implementation, the predeclared policy requires the planned
local gates and independent final acceptance before the real PR. No hosted CI is
claimed unless actually observed. Required CI that can run only after a PR exists
has a distinct pending state. Local-only artifact retention cannot recover another
machine, and no observed-base check guarantees that master will never move later.

## Policy decisions and current limitations

Recommended v1 choices: JSON; repository-local single active root; artifacts local
by default; origin/master as this repository's destination; PR opened as the normal
terminal outcome; fresh sequential agents; bounded retries; supported model fallback
only when recorded. Model availability and tool capabilities are checked per run.

Clarify artifact remote retention if recovery across machines is needed. A shared
artifacts branch and a shared key authority require distributed coordination beyond
the proposed local lock. CI-only-after-PR repositories need a separate CI-pending
state. Decide whether waiting for CI is part of the desired terminal outcome.

No skill-level promise of hostile-agent containment, autonomous wakeups after
process death, exhaustive test coverage, or correctness from model diversity.

## FOS-000026 — Include backlog completion in the implementation PR

**Status:** Done (verified proposed branch state; not landed on master).
**Completion evidence:** Independent unit checker passed 34/34 Python/Git tests with no skips, skill metadata validation, canonical-preservation review and historical PR #2 provenance checks. No C++/GPU/Steam coverage claimed; separate exact-candidate renewal and final review remain required. https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/compare/master...codex/FOS-000026-backlog-completion

**Depends on:** FOS-000025 (implementation merged in [PR #2](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/pull/2)).

### Problem

The harness records a completed run on `harness-artifacts`, but does not update
its canonical backlog items. A delivered task can therefore still say “in
progress,” as FOS-000025 currently does. Run completion is not reflected in the
backlog that future agents and contributors read.

### Required outcome

Add backlog completion as the final bookkeeping step on the implementation
branch, included in the same implementation PR as the task and its subtasks.
After the PR merges, the Done markers reach `master` with the implementation.
On an unmerged branch, Done describes that branch's verified proposed state;
it must not claim that the change has already landed on `master`.

This supersedes the earlier suggestion to wait for merge and then publish a
separate closeout change. Do not add a merge monitor, scheduler, direct write to
`master`, or separate closeout PR.

### Acceptance criteria

- Update the skill, role/state guidance and helper only as needed to make this
  a concrete final step. The planner decides the appropriate implementation and
  necessary test-suite additions using the [verification guide](../verification.md).
- Mark the root and each completed subtask Done in their canonical backlog
  definitions only after the applicable acceptance criteria and required
  verification pass. A parent stays incomplete while any required subtask or
  criterion remains open. Failed, unsupported, unavailable or incomplete required
  checks cannot justify Done.
- Preserve permanent keys, canonical definitions, dependencies and original
  acceptance criteria. Leave unfinished items open. Do not change allocation
  state in the permanent key registry to represent implementation completion.
- Retain concise verification evidence and an honest implementation-PR reference
  with the status update. Do not invent a PR number or claim a PR exists before
  creation. The planner must choose a reference that works with the publication
  order; a stable branch/compare reference is acceptable until an actual PR URL
  is known. Do not create an early PR solely to obtain a number.
- Include the bookkeeping changes in the final independently reviewed candidate.
  If source or backlog edits occur after review, invalidate/repeat the affected
  checks under the existing exact-commit rules. Publishing an unreviewed status
  commit must not bypass the checker or produce duplicate PRs.
- A checker rejection or later change that invalidates completion must also
  invalidate the corresponding Done claim. Interruption/resume must preserve
  unfinished closeout work rather than report successful bookkeeping that never
  happened.
- One implementation PR carries the root, subtasks and backlog updates. The
  harness never merges it automatically. Merging it is sufficient to update the
  backlog on `master`, with no subsequent closeout invocation required.
- Apply the resulting completion rule to this item in its implementation PR.
  Reconcile the stale FOS-000025 status only against its actual merged PR and
  retained verification evidence; do not mark other pending backlog work Done.

### Verification expectations

The planner owns the verification plan and test design; the implementer writes
and runs the planned tests; the checker independently validates their assertions
and execution. Cover a completed root, completed and incomplete subtasks, failed
mandatory verification, checker rejection after a proposed Done marker, and
interruption/resume before closeout is recorded. Verify that the reviewed
implementation PR includes the intended backlog edits and preserves keys and
acceptance text. Use behavioral tests for changed helper mechanics and realistic
isolated workflow checks for coordinator instructions; do not rely only on text
matching. Do not claim these future checks have already passed.

### Scope

Harness workflow, canonical backlog status/evidence, and meaningful verification.
No Fossilize C++ changes, automatic merge, background polling, retrospective
claims of unperformed verification, or unrelated backlog implementation.

## FOS-000027 — Commit and publish harness artifacts to the remote orphan branch

**Status:** Done (verified proposed branch state; not landed on master).
**Completion evidence:** Independent unit checker passed 51/51 Python/Git tests with no skips, metadata validation, original-criteria review and allocation-history counterexamples. Required exact-candidate renewal and separate final review follow bookkeeping; no C++/GPU/Steam coverage claimed. https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/compare/master...codex/FOS-000027-artifact-publication

**Depends on:** FOS-000025 (existing harness checkpoint and publication mechanics).

### Problem and reviewed evidence

Harness state, reports, evidence and allocation records remain in the local
`harness-artifacts` orphan history. A pushed implementation branch and an open PR
therefore do not make the run records available remotely.

Review on 2026-10-28 found that the installed `implement-change-harness` skill
explicitly selects local-only artifacts. Its `scripts/harness_state.py`
`checkpoint()` already writes a complete records tree with a temporary index,
creates a commit with `commit-tree`, and advances `refs/heads/harness-artifacts`
with an expected-tip `update-ref`. The publication workflow pushes the
implementation branch, but has no equivalent artifact publication step.
`git ls-remote --heads origin harness-artifacts` returned no branch, while the
local artifact tip was `5c0c6e5` (FOS-000026 publication revision 33).

The artifact inspection worktree can show modified/deleted records because ref
updates intentionally leave its index/files untouched; `references/state.md`
documents this. Its apparent dirtiness is not proof those records lack commits.
Inspect the committed tree rather than blindly staging that worktree or resetting
it. The original [proposal](../specs/basic-change-harness-plan.md) also specifies
local-only retention; this item deliberately changes that policy.

### Required outcome and acceptance criteria

- Make committing and publishing the allowed harness records to
  `origin`'s `refs/heads/harness-artifacts` part of the normal workflow. Record the
  repository/remote identity explicitly, keep the branch orphaned and separate
  from source history, and update the skill, state guidance and helper as needed.
- Define and enforce publication checkpoints covering initialization, state
  transitions and reports/evidence, permanent allocation changes, interruption
  and terminal run state. Distinguish locally committed from remotely confirmed
  records; retain a precise retry action when publication is incomplete. A run
  cannot claim successful artifact publication or full workflow completion while
  required records exist only locally.
- Publish the authoritative committed ref, including existing valid local run
  history. Preserve the records-only tree and existing validation. Do not stage
  stale inspection files, copy source trees, or include build outputs, binaries,
  private configuration, secrets or full transcripts. Preserve unexpected local
  edits when inspecting or refreshing a worktree.
- Use explicit non-force pushes to the recorded artifact destination. Verify the
  remote ref against the checkpoint being published; command success alone is
  insufficient. Never merge artifact history into the implementation PR or
  `master`, and never push to `upstream` merely because it exists.
- Handle an absent remote branch, already published checkpoints, remote advances
  and divergent history without overwriting either writer's work. Validate any
  adopted remote artifact history. Reconcile remote state before continuing;
  unresolved conflicts retain local records and a concrete recovery action.
  A repository-local lock must not be described as cross-machine coordination.
- Network/authentication/rejection failures and ambiguous push outcomes preserve
  the local checkpoint and remain recoverable. Resume checks the actual remote
  ref before retrying, without rerunning accepted implementation work, duplicating
  a PR or dropping allocation reservations. Define terminal publication ordering
  so the final state/active-pointer update is also published, without an endless
  cycle of commits acknowledging their own publication.

### Verification expectations

Use the [verification guide](../verification.md) to select meaningful behavioral
checks in isolated repositories with a bare remote. Cover first publication,
subsequent checkpoints, existing local history, idempotent retry, push rejection,
remote divergence, and interruption before/after a successful push but before its
acknowledgement. Fetch the artifact branch into a fresh clone and assert the
expected state, reports/evidence, allocation journal and terminal active pointer
are present in committed records. Check orphan ancestry, source/artifact separation
and preservation of stale inspection-worktree edits. Assert failed publication is
reported as incomplete and resume completes publication without recreating a PR.
These are future acceptance checks, not checks already performed for this item.

### Scope

Harness artifact persistence/publication, recovery, documentation and regression
coverage. No Fossilize C++ changes, automatic merge, background scheduler or claim
that remote retention alone solves distributed task-key allocation.
